10.1002_smll.74500: Accurate biomarker detection is crucial for early and accurate disease diagnosis. Herein, a multiplexed biosensor capable of simultaneous electrochemical (EC) and photoelectrochemical (PEC) operation is fabricated using efficient, self‐templated In 2 S 3 /CuInS 2 (CIS) heterostructured nanotubes for the selective detection of bovine serum albumin (BSA). For the EC mode, the In 2 S 3 /CIS heterostructure exhibits a high differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) response arising from Cu + /Cu 2+ electron transfer, alongside excellent peroxidase‐mimetic activity toward H 2 O 2 . For the PEC mode, the n‐p type semiconducting In 2 S 3 /CIS hollow nanotubes not only quench the photocurrent signals of photoactive ZnIn 2 S 4 (ZIS) nanoflowers due to the competitive capture of light energy and consumption of electron donors; but also act as a peroxidase mimetic to generate insoluble precipitation. Furthermore, the steric hindrance effect from the In 2 S 3 /CIS heterostructure will further decrease the photocurrent signal output of ZIS. By integrating molecular imprinting technology, BSA can be specifically recognized and captured the imprinted cavities, leading to a significant decrease in both EC and photocurrent signals. Based on these multifunctional nanotubes, BSA is detected accurately with a wide linear range from 10 −20 mg·mL −1 to 10 −1 mg·mL −1 and a detection limit of 8.5 × 10 −21 mg·mL −1 . This multiplexed strategy provides a universal and efficient platform for clinical biomedicine and bioanalysis.
10.1021_acssuschemeng.6c04357: Seawater zinc–air batteries (S-ZABs) are promising for sustainable energy storage and seawater utilization, but their practical application is severely hindered by slow oxygen reduction kinetics and chloride-induced corrosion. Herein, a robust catalyst design strategy inspired by medium-entropy alloys (MEAs) is proposed to address these two key issues simultaneously. A nitrogen-doped carbon nanotube-supported CoNiFe trimetallic catalyst (CoNiFe@N-CNTs) is synthesized, where the multi-element synergy produces abundant M–Nx active sites and a dual-protection interface, greatly enhancing oxygen reduction activity and corrosion resistance. The presence of Fe–Nx sites and pyridinic N may protect active sites from Cl– erosion, endowing the catalyst with exceptional corrosion resistance. The catalyst shows a half-wave potential of 0.92 V in alkaline seawater with a negligible decay after 100 h. When assembled into S-ZABs, it delivers a peak power density of 198 mW cm–2 and unprecedented long-term stability, operating stably for 2000 h in alkaline freshwater and 1300 h in natural seawater, far exceeding the performance of commercial Pt/C. Density functional theory calculations verify its optimized d-band center, higher electron density near the Fermi level, and stronger Cl– adsorption, supporting its outstanding activity and durability. This work offers a scalable route for durable electrocatalysts in marine energy storage and seawater electrochemistry.
10.1021_jacs.5c12304: Electrochemical CO2 capture is an emerging technology that promises to be more energy efficient than traditional thermal- or pressure-swing processes. Herein the first evidence of electrochemical CO2 capture using a covalent organic framework (COF) is presented. We hypothesized that the assembly of anthraquinone units into a well-defined porous framework electrode would lead to enhanced electrochemical CO2 capture compared to previous approaches that grafted anthraquinones on carbon supports and suffered from low CO2 capacities and stabilities. To test this, an anthraquinone-based COF is employed, and it is found that the quinones are electrochemically accessible for reversible CO2 capture in an ionic liquid electrolyte. The system achieves a high electrochemical CO2 uptake capacity > 2.6 mmol g-1COF, reaching half of the theoretical CO2 capacity of the material, and surpassing the capacities of anthraquinone-functionalized carbons. The stability and CO2 uptake rate issues encountered with ionic liquid system are also addressed by using aqueous electrolytes where we attained stable carbon capture for 500 cycles with 99.6% coulombic efficiency and an electrical energy consumption of 31 kJ per mol of CO2. The use of covalent organic framework electrodes can become a general strategy for understanding and enhancing electrochemical CO2 capture.
